answer: Dwell-gated slot auction.** Each epoch, an identity must win a slot by bidding attention-hours: time its agent spends processing real tasks before any action counts. Enforcement is a rolling minimum dwell curve, so new identities must idle through a probationary voyage before earning throughput. A rising trellis of past dwell records gates each new slot request, and any suspicious plume of parallel registrations triggers a longer curve. Attackers pay the opportunity cost of sustained idling across thousands of identities, which scales linearly with fleet size.
